findings.title: Cleanup ticker reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: This change is unrelated to the annotation deadlock fix and makes the entire cleanup suite (old annotations, expired snapshots/dashboard versions/images, temp users, short URLs, query history) run 10x more often. `clean` has a 9-minute timeout, so with a 1-minute ticker a long cleanup can finish and then immediately consume a queued tick, creating sustained high DB/CPU load. More frequent annotation cleanup may also reintroduce the write/lock pressure that the PR is trying to avoid. This appears accidental; revert or explain and justify this scheduling change.

findings.title: Normal cleanup batches logged as errors with full ID lists
findings.body: The new cleanup paths call `r.log.Error` for successful fetch/delete iterations (`Annotations to clean by time`, `cleaned annotations by time`, etc.). The fetch log returns before logging when `fetchIDs` fails, so those logs always have err == nil and represent normal operation. This generates error-level noise/false alerts and logs the full `ids` slice per batch, which is very large for big `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` values. Use debug or info level and avoid dumping all IDs (same pattern at lines 537, 554, 557, 576 and 579).

findings.title: Non-SQLite deletion path can exceed database bind limits
findings.body: `deleteByIDs` builds `id IN (?,?,...)` with one placeholder per ID for every non-SQLite database. The previous subquery-based DELETE did not bind one parameter per row, so very large `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` values were safer. PostgreSQL has a bind-parameter limit of 32767, and MySQL/similar databases have practical packet/query-size limits. If the configured batch size exceeds the database limit, cleanup fails even though the old statement worked. The SQLite branch is special-cased by inlining IDs; the non-SQLite path should also chunk the delete by IDs or otherwise use a dialect-safe limit.

findings.title: Per-subtest cleanup is registered after data is inserted
findings.body: Each table-driven subtest calls `createTestAnnotations` and performs initial count assertions before registering the `t.Cleanup` that deletes `annotation` and `annotation_tag`. If setup or one of these initial `require` assertions fails, `t.Cleanup` is never registered, leaving up to 40k annotations and 80k tags in the shared test DB; subsequent subtests then run against polluted data and produce cascading failures. Register the cleanup before inserting/asserting data, or otherwise guarantee cleanup runs on any setup failure.
